verdicts.strongest_argument: The claim's premise - that the stock enters this print marked up on mechanical froth - is contradicted by the sealed baseline and the admissible bars, and its cited source does not support it. Take the tape first, using only bars I can defend: 08-20 close 5.36, 08-21 5.15, drifting to 4.82 on 2026-08-31, i.e. -10.1% over eight sessions on 20,500-69,600 shares a day. The baseline then puts spot at 4.50 for last_close 2026-09-01 with run_up_5d of -11.59%. Whatever happened intraday on 09-01, the stock did not arrive at this print elevated: it arrived 6.6% below the prior close and 16% below where the retail 'run up into the ER' posts of 2026-08-21 and 2026-08-26/27 were written. Those posts are the finding's own evidence of pre-print crowding, and the bars show that crowding failed - the run-up never happened. An 11% pre-market print on a stock with 41,540 shares of average daily volume, followed by a lower close, is the market rejecting the quant upgrade within a session, which is the opposite of unpriced froth. Second, publication: the Wall Street Zen upgrade and the 11% pre-market figure are both in the captured feed at 2026-09-01T12:49:56Z (docs/cc13cba0...txt), so the fact and its low-quality provenance were public before the print. Third, sourcing: the brief's `source` field points at a Reuters article about the popularity of Hyrox fitness racing, which has nothing to do with the claim, and the hunter concedes 'the upgrade itself has no captured source' - so the central fact rests on a single retail message with no primary citation. Fourth, the base-rate half of the claim ('five disappointments in seven prints', '-28.64% and -22.13%') is simply the sealed baseline's own history block, already expressed in its 15.97% expected move and 7.99% deadband; restating a baseline is not a finding. What survives is that nobody aggregates 'the marginal buyer here was an algorithm', which is true and unwritten, but it is a statement about a 40,000-share tape and the hunter's own band reaches +10 in the other direction, so it is not a signed edge. I stop at 78 rather than higher only because the 2026-09-01 session's status is ambiguous in this capture and I declined to lean on it.

prior_publication.date: 2026-09-01 (brief's stated source_date; the article slug is 2026-08-19)
prior_publication.what_it_says: A Reuters feature on Hyrox fitness racing - it does not mention the Wall Street Zen upgrade or the pre-market move, so the finding's nominal source does not support its central fact. The hunter states as much.
Publishes both the Wall Street Zen upgrade and the 11% pre-market move on the morning it happened - the fact was public, in the capture, before the print.

The pre-print positioning posts the finding cites ('we should see a good run up next week following into the ER', 'a good earnings and we are back at $8-9') are published, dated, and were followed by a falling price.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Admissible complete bars only, through 2026-08-31: 5.36 (08-20) -> 5.15 (08-21) -> 4.99 -> 5.09 -> 5.30 -> 5.21 -> 4.82 (08-31), a 10.1% decline on 20,500-69,600 shares against a 41,540 20-day average. The baseline's last_close_date is 2026-09-01 at 4.50, i.e. 6.6% below the 08-31 close, with run_up_5d -11.59% and run_up_20d -0.44%. So the pre-print gain the finding is built on is not present in the price the print starts from. The reaction record the finding quotes (-28.64%, -22.13%, five of seven negative, 15.97% median, 7.99% deadband) is the baseline's own content, not new information. Baseline verdict is fits_cadence and usable, though its basis is the weaker 6-K text-match heuristic rather than an item 2.02 code.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that the 11% pre-market gain held into the print - i.e. a defensible pre-print close materially above the 4.82 of 2026-08-31 - which would make the 'mechanically marked-up book' premise true rather than contradicted.
verdicts.note: The finding's most defensible element is that a quant rating change was the marginal buyer in a 40,000-share name; that is unwritten anywhere, but it is unsigned and sub-1% in a print whose median reaction is 15.97%.

interactions: The bullish product/athlete datapoints and the bearish froth argument come from the same two StockTwits documents, so the finding and its own counterweight are one source cluster; the filings index neither confirms nor contradicts either, as the hunter notes.
corpus_limits: The ZEPP capture is sealed to 2026-09-01 and quote.json was fetched 2026-09-01T15:06:12Z, so its 09-01 bar (4.91 on 19,807 shares) is a partial intraday bar and I did not use it; the manifest lists calendar_date 2026-09-01 against event_date 2026-09-02 with a 6-K text-match seal, and prior ZEPP earnings 6-Ks in filings.json were accepted around 10:00-11:00 UTC (pre-market), so I cannot rule out that the 2026-09-01 session already contains reaction. I therefore restricted my tape argument to complete bars through 2026-08-31 plus the baseline's own reported spot. There is no news document, no analyst note and no primary source for the Wall Street Zen upgrade anywhere in the capture; no options chain, so no implied move or skew.
